Robot equations, wind mapping, reference generation, and checks

Wind velocity → force → acceleration

ṗ = v
v̇ = u + aair(p,v)
vrelative = wxy(p) − v
Fair = c ‖vrelative‖ vrelative
aair = Fair / m
m = 0.680 kg · c = 0.1 kg/m
−1.6 ≤ uₓ, uᵧ ≤ 1.6 m/s²

The nominal robot is a planar double integrator. The existing quadratic air-force law maps relative horizontal air velocity into an added acceleration. This robot uses the revised airflow shown above, with the same column and monitoring-region geometry. These mass and drag parameters come from the repository; they are a designed robot model, not a calibration to a measured vehicle.

The robot uses the fixed horizontal velocity slice at 0.75 m, with the same cell-center bilinear interpolation as the wind display. Vertical and attitude dynamics are outside this planar model. Still air sets w = 0 and retains the same air-force law.

Reference and tracker

The three route guides define smooth C² geometric curves. A quintic time law starts and ends at rest, with speed ≤ 1 m/s and reference acceleration ≤ 0.8 m/s² per axis. Both directions traverse the same curve. Timing depends on geometry, not on wind or which controller succeeds.

unom = clip[aref + 1.2(pref−p) + 1.8(vref−v), ±1.6]

Both conditions use this same tracker without wind feedforward. Each runs for the reference duration plus 10 s holding the goal. No replanning or belief-adaptive method is used.

Full RPCBF diagnostic

The existing flow-policy RPCBF uses bounded braking with air-force compensation as its backup policy, 8 backup steps of 0.15 s, full not-a-knot cubic-spline extrema, state derivatives through the rollouts, and the original constrained QP. Safety margin: 0.06 m. Backup gain: 2 s⁻¹. Barrier gain: 1 s⁻¹.

This first comparison gives the filter the known wind field. Its three construction fields are identical because uncertainty is zero. It is a known-wind diagnostic, not a learned-belief or uncertainty-robust evaluation. The robot remains a point; the drawing’s dot is a position marker.

The actuator box stays hard. If barrier constraints are infeasible, the original minimum-slack backup is used and the step is counted as infeasible. Contact stops integration; it is never hidden or replaced with a bounce.

Numerical checks

Control and filtering run every 0.05 s. Held-control RK4 integrates at 0.01 s and samples the spatial wind at every RK4 stage. Contact is checked along each substep. Browser playback interpolates these computed records only.

Loading verification…

The wind fields retain their provisional CFD status above. These runs demonstrate the robot’s response to those specific fields; they do not establish validated physical wind, global safety, or route impossibility.

With an initial wind survey

05 / TASK-DIRECTED EXPLORATION

Learn wind when it improves the decision

Can sacrificing some monitoring now produce better decisions later? This added experiment evaluates future wind measurements through their effect on the next physical trajectory and its monitoring cost.

300 s · Bayesian look-ahead

Useful learning

A measurement can change the next route, traversal speed, tracking or safety. Its benefit must outweigh the monitoring lost while obtaining it.

Irrelevant wind uncertainty

If learning cannot improve the physical path or monitoring outcome, there is no exploration reward. No entropy, novelty or uncertainty-reduction bonus is added.

Observed outcome: Loading the completed comparison and its limitations…

Matched comparison: both methods plan with wind and learn from their actual measurements. The left forecast anticipates a measurement-dependent continuation; the right forecast freezes its current belief. The earlier still-air baseline, surveyed runs and all animations remain above.

Three prefixes, one hypothetical measurement branch, one conditional wind sample and four continuation choices form an explicitly bounded planning approximation. This small sample budget limits statistical confidence.

What was tested, including unsuccessful approaches

Decision relevance checks

Controlled decision-rule tests cover four cases: irrelevant wind does not justify a sensing detour; useful measurements can repay an initial task cost; freezing the belief removes that benefit; and excessive exploration cost causes rejection. These tests check the selector’s logic. The recorded physical missions below are the performance evidence.

Limits of the current result

A correct information objective alone does not establish that these constrained robot/filter dynamics can reach A. The finite horizon, restricted continuation library and sparse posterior can all limit progress. Failed route behavior remains visible.

06 / ONLINE SURVEY AND MONITORING

Survey useful routes while maintaining clarity

Wind uncertainty helps construct geometric starts. Exploration must justify its monitoring cost through a predicted benefit on useful routes. Actual observations update the wind belief along the executed path.

300 s · online survey

Learning must repay its cost

Three paired route forecasts estimate whether knowing the wind could reduce monitoring cost. Route-specific covariance reduction converts that estimate into a bounded learning reward. The planner balances this reward against clarity deficit.

Measurements need representation

The same 128-variable POAM model now protects inducing points at acquired measurement locations. Full residual covariance and accumulated statistics remain present. Both methods below share this allocation policy.

PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT8 × 4.625 × 2 m

Three circular columns, 1.5 m high

AIR20°C · 1.204 kg/m³

Molecular viscosity from air temperature

COMPUTATIONLoading grid…

3D MRT lattice Boltzmann · Smagorinsky LES

DISPLAYHeight 0.75 m

One fixed field · no time loop or gusts

Constant in time does not mean uniform in space

Speed and direction at any location stay the same for the entire animation. They can differ between locations. Zero wind is allowed; no minimum wind speed is imposed. Only the particle positions change.

What this model establishes

The stationary fields come from the vector mean of a 3D CFD calculation under constant inlet conditions. Sheltering and wakes are computed around the obstacles. Numerical accuracy and robot impassability are separate checks; neither is assumed.

Wind definition, physical setup, and numerical checks

Time-independent environment

w(x, y) = ⟨u(x, y, z = 0.75 m, τ)⟩
∂w/∂t = 0
Particle motion: ẋ = wₓ(x, y), ẏ = wᵧ(x, y)

The background is one fixed vector field per scenario. The CFD generation uses a constant inlet, discards its startup interval, and averages velocity vectors over 16–32 s. The animation never plays those transient CFD frames. This is a mean-flow environment; instantaneous turbulent fluctuations are outside the requested stationary model.

Three-dimensional CFD used to construct the field

∂u/∂t + (u · ∇)u = −∇p/ρ + ∇ · [2(ν + νₜ)S]
∇ · u ≈ 0 in the low-Mach numerical limit
S = ½(∇u + ∇uᵀ),   νₜ = (0.16 Δ)² √(2S:S)

The model uses the published lbmpy Smagorinsky LES implementation with a D3Q19 multiple-relaxation-time collision operator. Small eddies below the mesh size are modeled. This is isothermal, low-Mach airflow; near-wall turbulence is not fully resolved by this grid.

Air viscosity is μ = 1.458 × 10⁻⁶ T³ᐟ² / (T + 110.4) Pa·s. At T = 293.15 K, ν = μ/ρ ≈ 1.506 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s. Molecular viscosity is not increased to make the computation easier.

Boundary and initial conditions

Loading the exact physical boundary conditions…

Wind inside monitoring regions

Loading before/after wind measurements…

The monitoring rectangles and circular columns have the same sizes and locations. The redesign changes airflow boundary conditions. Residual circulation and small faster patches near the passage edges remain; the regions are not forced to exactly zero wind.

Geometry and numerical resolution

The sketch sets the circular footprints. Cylinder boundaries use analytic circle/link intersections. At obstacle/floor and overlapping-cylinder junctions where the interpolation lacks a second fluid node, the library-prescribed halfway no-slip treatment is used and counted in the configuration. This finite-grid treatment is not exact surface geometry at those links. Loading numerical resolution… The CFD sampling interval is approximately 0.1 s.

Loading numerical checks…

The displayed streamlets use spatial interpolation of a single fixed horizontal velocity field. They visualize a horizontal slice; they are not full 3D particle trajectories. The particle-speed control affects only animation timing. The heatmap and wind vectors remain unchanged.

Robot model remains separate

The nominal robot remains a double integrator, ṗ = v, v̇ = u. The robot comparison adds an explicit air-force acceleration. The CFD output is air velocity in m/s; it has not been substituted directly for the robot’s acceleration disturbance. The robot comparison above now maps this air velocity to force and acceleration with the existing quadratic air-force law. The separate monitoring comparison above adds planning under the learned wind belief.
